summary.headline: SG Mart Q1 FY27: service centres volume 160,000 tons (up from 121,000 YoY); management reiterates ~INR300 crore FY27 EBITDA target.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the second consecutive quarter of sustained revenue and profitability, with an EBITDA margin of more than 4% helped by higher realisations from steel prices (up INR2,500-3,000/ton) and a mix shift toward special-coated steel products. Service centre volumes fell QoQ on seasonality but rose YoY, and management said Q2 should pick up. Capex was INR90 crore in Q1, with INR400-500 crore planned for FY27 and about INR1,500 crore over 2-3 years, which management says will be funded internally. Management flagged geopolitical and oil-price risk as the main variable to the guidance.

financial_highlights.change: up from 121,000 tons YoY; down QoQ on seasonality

financial_highlights.value: more than 4% (cited as ~4.5% on the call)

financial_highlights.change: from INR284 crore at 31 March 2026 (Q1 call figure; INR283 crore cited later)

segments.name: Service centres
segments.commentary: Q1 volume 160,000 tons, EBITDA ~INR1,800-2,000/ton; 7 centres fully operational, 12 targeted in 6-12 months and 25 by 2029-30. Each centre: ~INR50 crore gross block, 8,000 tons/month, ~INR500 crore annual revenue.

segments.name: Steel profiles
segments.commentary: Q1 volume 18,000 tons (run-rate ~75,000 tons); installed capacity ~200,000 tons; EBITDA ~INR3,000-4,000/ton on purchased coated steel.

segments.name: Renewable (solar) structures
segments.commentary: Q1 volume ~11,000 tons (run-rate ~50,000 tons); capacity ~200,000 tons; EBITDA ~INR3,000-3,500/ton; order book 2-3 months, project-specific; contributes little revenue today.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: Two products launched, revenue ramp-up started; margins described as potentially double-digit. No quantified numbers given.

segments.name: B2B metal trading
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 17,000 tons; management says full-year volume ~60,000 tons, no investment required, not a focus area.

guidance_outlook: FY27 absolute EBITDA target of ~INR300 crore, reiterated, conditional on no sharp macro deterioration.
No quarterly EBITDA percentage or per-ton guidance; blended EBITDA/ton may fall as service-centre mix rises, but absolute EBITDA expected to rise each quarter.
Management cites a 50% CAGR target over three years (per analyst question); 2030 vision of INR25,000-35,000 crore revenue and minimum INR1,000 crore EBITDA on 4+ million tons.

Backward-integrated coated-steel (CRM and metal coating) line at Raipur expected in ~18 months, lifting steel profile and solar margins to above INR5,000/ton, and by INR3,000-4,000/ton per management.
Seven new products in pipeline for launch over next two quarters; contract manufacturing to be detailed in Q2 call.
Management says no new capital raise or dilution needed; capex funded by existing cash plus operating cash flow.
capex_capacity: Capex ~INR90 crore in Q1 FY27; INR400-500 crore planned for FY27; ~INR1,500 crore total over 2-3 years, of which INR700 crore already on books.
Plan to add 15-18 service centres at ~INR50 crore each (~INR900 crore); land and build-out typically 9-15 months per centre.
Raipur backward-integration (cold rolling and coating) line: land acquired, construction begun, some machinery ordered; expected operational in ~18 months.
Profiling capacity: ~400,000 tons across steel profiles and solar structures versus ~120,000 tons annualised run-rate; accessories to use idle space at existing service centres.
Service centre target: 25 by 2029-30, adding 5 per year.
demand_pricing: Steel prices rose INR2,500-3,000/ton between 1 April and 30 June 2026; special-coated products realise INR10,000-15,000/ton above average HR-coil-based products.
Customer base described as wide: service centre customers are SMEs/MSMEs and small traders, not large OEMs; solar structures sold to a limited set of top 20-30 EPCs/IPPs.
New value-added products are said to be acquiring entirely new customers rather than wallet share from existing trading customers.
Management sees itself as the only organised pan-India service-centre player; solar and steel profile competition is from fragmented small profilers.
Analysts asked about inventory gains; management said inventory gains were minimal as inventory fell in absolute terms.

qa_highlights.question: Was the margin improvement structural or driven by inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed NSR gains to steel price rises and mix shift to special-coated products, said inventory gains were minimal, and declined to guide quarterly EBITDA percentage.

qa_highlights.question: What are the service centre economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Each centre needs ~INR50 crore gross block plus INR25-30 crore working capital, sells ~8,000 tons/month (~INR500 crore/year) at ~INR2,000/ton EBITDA, implying ~INR20 crore EBITDA on INR75-80 crore capital employed.

qa_highlights.question: What are EBITDA per ton figures by segment and are Q1 numbers one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Service centres INR1,800-2,000/ton; steel profiles INR3,000-4,000/ton; solar structures INR3,000-3,500/ton; post-backward integration above INR5,000/ton. Management said Q1 profitability is regular business, not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the target move from 30 to 25 service centres and are there execution challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the number matters less than pan-India cluster coverage; Q1 volume was up 32% YoY (121,000 to 160,000 tons) and the QoQ dip was seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 EBITDA target of INR300 crore still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was set in the Q4 call and remains achievable given Q1 momentum, unless macro deteriorates; cited Iran-US conflict and oil-price rebound as risks.

qa_highlights.question: Will contract manufacturing dilute ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no vertical would be allowed to dilute ROCE below 20%, with the group aspiring to above 25%.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and oil-price volatility (Iran-US conflict cited); management said a sustained shock could hit customer industries within 2-3 weeks.
Working capital: trade payables declined and steel advances rose to INR211 crore; working capital days (27) need to fall to 20-25 days as targeted.
Execution on 15-18 new service centres and Raipur coated-steel line; timeline slippage would affect the margin uplift.
Blended EBITDA per ton may fall as lower-margin service-centre mix rises, with no quarterly margin guidance.
Disclosure inconsistencies on the call: inventory cited as INR284 crore and INR283 crore; 50% CAGR target and 'Q1 EBITDA margin 4.5%' were not clearly stated by management.
Contract manufacturing and new categories still undefined; details promised for Q2 call.
Segment EBITDA not disclosed; an analyst requested it and management agreed to work on it.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term build-out, with the 2030 vision and product pipeline stressed. Cautious and hedged on near-term items: no quarterly EBITDA percentage guidance, macro risk flagged repeatedly, and the answer on order book and capex was specific but limited.
key_quotes: So right now, the idea in SG Mart is to create a manufacturing platform with ability to sell in own brand through network of service centers and our own distribution network.

So I will not guide EBITDA percentage right now, Vishal, like quarter-on-quarter because in next quarter, say, in quarter 2, if the service centre business picks up, which was pretty slow in quarter 1
So what matters is that are we covering pan-India? Are we covering each and every industrial cluster in Indian state?
But what I can tell you is that any vertical, we will not dilute ROCE below 20%, no matter what.
